I can't say whether you're "good." I can tell you what the checklist's lines show against your files. The checklist audit ran on 2026-11-03, on readings dated 2026-10-14. Anything you added after 2026-10-14 was not seen.

**The most urgent item is the permit renewal (lines A1 and A2).**
- The Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit says it expires November 15, 2026. The audit word for A1 is out of date. That is not the same as expired.
- Condition 1.3 sets the renewal application deadline at July 18, 2026. The audit word for A2 is nothing on file. That means we have not been shown it. It does not mean it wasn't filed.
- If you filed on time, upload the application and DEQ's receipt. The permit's Condition 1.2 refers to a timely renewal application when it covers operating after expiry.
- If you did not file, the finding says operations must stop on November 15, 2026. Please contact DEQ now.

**Other lines**

| Line | Audit word | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| A3 annual report | on file | The Annual Report, Reporting Year 2025, has a DEQ receipt dated February 12, 2026. |
| A4 semi-annual report | nothing on file | The January–June 2026 report was due July 31, 2026. We have not been shown it. |
| A5 deviations | on file | The 2025 annual report covers the August 2025 S-2 pump failure. The September 9, 2026 S-2 reading of 6.4 (limit 6.0) has no note about DEQ notice. |
| B1 daily scrubber log | on file | The Scrubber Pressure-Drop Log has no readings for August 17–21. It has no September operating-day totals. |
| B2 quarterly inspections | nothing on file | The records are not among your documents. |
| B3 carbon replacement | nothing on file | The annual report set March 14, 2026, and no vendor record is on file. |
| B4 weekly detector-tube checks | on file | The week of September 14 is missing. |
| B5 opacity records | nothing on file | No records or method statement have been shown. |
| B6 five-year retention | on file | This rests only on the annual report's receipt. |
| C1 | on file | Pressure drop is read from the log, not from the day. |
| C2, C3 | not a document question | These are checked in person. |
| C4 employee count | on file | The Emergency Action Plan says 42 employees, dated 2021-02-01. You declared 38 enterprise-wide. These two numbers disagree, so check the current count before fee-tier questions. |
| C5 emergency plan | on file | The plan is marked Needs work. It does not name the incident coordinator. |

**Other points**
- Nobody has signed the log for August or September. The Notes column for September 9 is blank.
- The September 9 reading may need DEQ notice under the permit's deviation condition (5.2: 24 hours, then written report in 15 days). Check that condition.
- The checklist is only DEQ's air permit form. The audit also lists some items as suggestions, not findings. These are things companies like yours usually hold, which we have not been shown: Tier II inventory, hazardous waste records, stormwater coverage, and a HazCom program.

I suggest running the Oregon DEQ audit again after you upload the renewal application, the semi-annual report and the carbon record.
